### Anniston

- **Type:** City
- **Recorded status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-08-18, Anniston City Council adopted Resolution No. 26-R-97. AL.com reported that the vote was unanimous. [VERIFY: agenda amendment remains unverified.]
- **Normalized date:** `2026-08-18` (exact)
- **Duration:** 12 months, effective immediately; council may shorten or extend. Planning Commission to report recommendations within six months.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `al-anniston-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Resolution No. 26-R-97 (temporary moratorium on the permitting, development and licensing of data centers within the city's regulatory jurisdiction)
- **What prompted it:** The resolution adopts the Planning Commission recommendation and identifies possible inadequacies in existing zoning and concerns including electrical demand, water and wastewater, stormwater, noise, lighting, generators and neighborhood compatibility. AL.com reported that the city already had a 2 MW FirmFarm colocation facility; the facility’s treatment under the moratorium is not established.
- **Affected projects:** The resolution exempts issuance of business licenses to currently operating businesses, unless operation ceases for 60 days or more or an expired license was not timely renewed. This is not an established blanket exemption from all permitting/development restrictions.
- **Detailed status:** Resolution 26-R-97 was adopted 2026-08-18, effective immediately for twelve months subject to council shortening or extension. WBRC reported the pause on 2026-08-27. [VERIFY: September 23 status, later actions and current force remain unverified.]
- **Outcome:** One-year moratorium adopted.

### HB399 (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `al-hb399-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** House authors: Hulsey, Rafferty, Tillman, Mooney, DuBose, Carns, Robertson, Hammett, Crow, Stringer, Brinyark, Kirkland, Bedsole; joint sponsor: Jones (as listed by the Secretary of State act docket); [VERIFY: retained historical party classification Mixed-party; individual affiliations and lead designation not independently established.]
- **Recorded status:** Approved by Governor 2026-04-16 (Act 2026-573); ALISON records Enacted 2026-04-17; stated effective 2026-06-01.
- **Provisions:** Amends Alabama data-processing-center tax abatements and sales-tax distribution. For qualifying abatements granted on or after January 1, 2027, revised duration tiers generally permit up to 20 years, with a conditional additional 10 years for qualified local investments. For centers with at least 100 MW peak demand, specified state noneducational ad valorem and construction-related transaction tax abatements generally end when property is placed in service, subject to eligible equipment and targeted-county gubernatorial exceptions. Extends the incentive application sunset and excludes specified incentives in projects executed before the effective date and expansions of those projects during the following ten years from the amendments to Sections 40-9B-3, 40-9B-4 and 40-9B-4.1. Act effective June 1, 2026.
- **Mechanism / scope:** incentive_restriction; fiscal
- **Legal effect:** unknown
- **Effective date:** 2026-06-01
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/files/pdf/SearchableInstruments/2026RS/HB399-enr.pdf>)

### HB403 (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `al-hb403-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Representatives Rafferty, Hulsey, Tillman (engrossed bill author line; given-name identities not independently established); Mixed-party (Rafferty is Democrat; Hulsey/Tillman are Republicans) [VERIFY: partisan composition not separately confirmed]
- **Recorded status:** House passed as amended and engrossed 2026-03-17; this is the latest action in the ALISON history returned 2026-11-07 and independently re-observed 2026-11-09. Earlier record claimed death at sine die without Senate floor action and identified SB270 as companion vehicle; those claims remain unverified. The official Legislature site identifies April 9, 2026 as adjournment of the 2026 Regular Session; the bill-specific terminal consequence remains unresolved.
- **Provisions:** Engrossed proposal would add public-interest review criteria for retail electric service contracts with large-load customers, including incremental cost recovery and positive benefits to other customers. Its large-load-customer definition uses expected peak demand of 100 MW or greater at one or more contiguous parcels and is not confined to data processing centers. The text separately uses the term large load data center customer in the incremental-cost definition; that wording difference is not silently normalized.
- **Mechanism / scope:** utility_large_load_restriction; utility_grid
- **Legal effect:** unknown
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/files/pdf/SearchableInstruments/2026RS/HB403-eng.pdf>)

### SB265 (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `al-sb265-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Senators Jones, Waggoner, Kitchens, Kelley, Smitherman, Singleton, Chesteen, Bell, Albritton, Melson, Butler, Allen, Stewart, Figures, Coleman-Madison, Williams, Gudger (engrossed bill author line); [VERIFY: retained historical party classification Republican lead; individual affiliations and lead designation not independently established.]

The official Legislature site identifies April 9, 2026 as adjournment of the 2026 Regular Session; the bill-specific terminal consequence remains unresolved.
- **Provisions:** Senate engrossed proposal would revise data-center tax abatements and sales-tax distribution, including maximum exemption periods and limits on certain state tax abatements for centers at or above 100 MW for abatements granted on or after January 1, 2027, with equipment and targeted-county exceptions. It extends the incentive application sunset and includes a transitional provision for certain pre-effective projects and expansions in a Class 3 municipality. A distinct House substitute was reported and offered; its adoption is not established.

### SB270 (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `al-sb270-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Senate author: Bell; joint sponsor: Rafferty (as listed by the Secretary of State act docket); Republican [VERIFY: retained historical classification; author identity and party not independently confirmed in reopened sources.]
- **Recorded status:** Approved by Governor 2026-04-16 (Act 2026-610); ALISON records Enacted 2026-04-17; stated effective 2026-10-01.
- **Provisions:** Adds Ala. Code Section 37-4-22.1. Defines a large load data center customer as a contracted retail customer with expected peak demand of at least 150 MW on contiguous parcels, meeting the statutory data processing center definition and operating solely for data processing. PSC public-interest review considers recovery of incremental costs and positive benefits to other retail customers.
